why.Home Lake basecamp, from either the Dung: When you want a relaxed two-day trip with a camp a mile from the cirque, or you are linking the neighbouring peaks from the same lake; the Dosewallips side is longer and rarely used.

review.notes: Dungeness/Boulder Camp is the standard approach; Home Lake is a camp option on the same corridor, and the Dosewallips side is longer due to the road washout.

why.The unmarked SR-20 turnout, then a boot: When you want a boot path that reaches the true south ridge rather than cross-country timber from the PCT lot; it is about the same gain and a touch longer.

review.notes: Searches describe the SR-20 turnout boot path as a main route; stored notes call the PCT lot the most used. Evidence is mixed, mark left alone.

problems: Online descriptions lead with the SR-20 turnout boot path (the true south ridge) as the main route, while the stored mark has the Rainy Pass PCT lot as Most used. Owner may want to check which is truly more common.

why.Snow Gulch direct (deep snow only): Early season with deep snow burying the slide alder, mostly for ski parties; it saves distance but is a steep bushwhack with overhead slide hazard in poor snow.

review.notes: Ski reports describe about 800 ft of bushwhack in Snow Gulch, miserable in ski boots without enough snow; Niederprum remains the standard.

why.Around the East Face and through the Gap: When arriving from climbs on the far side of the formation, since it links both sides without going back to the car; otherwise it is longer than walking up the road.

review.notes: Online search found no usable page for this crag's approaches; the reason is taken from the stored notes, which state it plainly.
fromStoredNotes: Around the East Face and through the Gap

why.Windy Creek trail from Cathedral Drivewa: Shortest way up, for parties who want to avoid the longer drive to Long Swamp, though the trail is less used and overgrown in stretches.
why.Boundary Trail from Iron Gate: To make it a longer loop that returns over Sunny Pass, or to link with Horseshoe Basin; the road to the trailhead is rough and wants high clearance.

review.notes: Long Swamp trailhead is the usual start for Windy Peak; Iron Gate is the loop start; Windy Creek is the shortest but less maintained. Primary already marked.
